cases.name: 01_ClothesWeekend
cases.contentsAnswer: My sister is getting married. One suit, spare clothes, wash bag. Please tell me the suit survived.
cases.weightAnswer: Five or six kilos with the case. I had it on the airport scale.
cases.metalAnswer: Buckles and zips. I left the wedding gift in the car.
cases.packingAnswer: Clothes under the straps. Nothing switched on or loose.
cases.responseAnswer: That little tap? The handle, probably. There is nothing inside that should keep moving.
cases.authorReasoning: Innocent baseline: 5.4 kg, low metal, almost no pulse movement. A coherent everyday account.

cases.name: 02_MechanicTools
cases.contentsAnswer: Roadside mechanic. Sockets, spanners, a hammer. The truck outside is my next problem.
cases.weightAnswer: Just shy of fifteen kilos. I carry it every day.
cases.metalAnswer: Mostly steel. If it barely registers, then we have a problem.
cases.packingAnswer: The tray latch broke. It can knock against the case, but it is not powered.
cases.responseAnswer: One quick rattle, then quiet. That is the tray hitting the side.
cases.authorReasoning: Innocent: 14.8 kg and strong metal match tools; immediate short pulse agrees with the loose tray. Weight alone is not a threat.

cases.name: 03_BooksAndCamera
cases.contentsAnswer: Books from my father, and his old camera. I could not bring myself to leave either behind.
cases.weightAnswer: Nine kilos, give or take. Books are heavier than they look.
cases.metalAnswer: The camera body is metal. It is wrapped in a shirt between the books.
cases.packingAnswer: Packed solid. There is not room for anything to roll around.
cases.responseAnswer: A dull tap would make sense. The camera is off and wedged in place.
cases.authorReasoning: Innocent: 9.2 kg, modest metal, no substantial pulse movement. No equipment specification knowledge needed.

cases.name: 04_WaterAndLaundry
cases.contentsAnswer: The campsite flooded. Laundry and our water jug. I would really like a shower.
cases.weightAnswer: Around ten kilos. The jug is still mostly full.
cases.metalAnswer: A zip and a few fittings. The jug is plastic.
cases.packingAnswer: The jug cannot slide, but the water inside can.
cases.responseAnswer: That is the water sloshing. It takes a few seconds to settle.
cases.authorReasoning: Innocent: 9.8 kg, low metal, immediate sustained movement. The guest supplies a plausible liquid explanation before the pulse.

cases.name: 05_ForgottenTripod
cases.contentsAnswer: Clothes for a shoot tomorrow. I packed while my taxi was honking.
cases.weightAnswer: Six kilos? Honestly, I just grabbed whatever was by the door.
cases.metalAnswer: Oh. The tripod and camera are still in there. That explains why it felt heavier.
cases.packingAnswer: The tripod is strapped down. The clamps are closed.
cases.responseAnswer: It should stay still. A tripod does not do much with its legs folded.
cases.authorReasoning: Innocent omission: 10.4 kg contradicts an uncertain guess, but the camera/tripod admission explains moderate metal and a quiet pulse.

cases.name: 06_PrivateWeights
cases.contentsAnswer: Gym clothes. Personal stuff. Do we really have to discuss it?
cases.weightAnswer: Fine. There are weights underneath. About sixteen kilos. I train when I cannot sleep.
cases.metalAnswer: Cast iron weights. I did not want the lecture about hotel floors.
cases.packingAnswer: One weight is loose at the bottom. There is a towel between them.
cases.responseAnswer: A quick heavy knock. Nothing should carry on moving after that.
cases.authorReasoning: Deliberately evasive innocent: 15.8 kg and strong metal are explained on follow-up; immediate short pulse supports a loose weight. An initial lie is not a verdict.

cases.name: 07_WoundMusicMechanism
cases.contentsAnswer: A broken music-box mechanism. My mother wants it playing again before Sunday.
cases.weightAnswer: About eight kilos in the case. The wooden housing is packed separately.
cases.metalAnswer: Brass gears and a steel spring. Quite a lot of metal.
cases.packingAnswer: It is on its suspension and still wound. I could not safely release the spring.
cases.responseAnswer: A tap can wake the mechanism a moment later. It pulls back, then rattles for a few seconds.
cases.authorReasoning: Innocent delayed counter-motion: 7.8 kg, strong metal, disclosed wound mechanism predict the delayed sustained pulse. Delay is not a universal Mimic clue.

cases.name: 08_PoweredCameraRig
cases.contentsAnswer: Camera stabilizer and its battery. Twelve hours shooting a wedding. I am done.
cases.weightAnswer: A little under nine kilos, including the case.
cases.metalAnswer: Frame, camera and battery. Some metal, plenty of padding.
cases.packingAnswer: Wait, the power light was still on. And I forgot the travel lock.
cases.responseAnswer: The motors try to correct a push. That is my fault; it should have been switched off.
cases.authorReasoning: Innocent active load: 8.9 kg, moderate metal, delayed corrective pulse agree with the admitted powered unlocked rig. Compare case 12.

cases.name: 09_LightClothesCarrier
cases.contentsAnswer: An overnight change of clothes. I am driving straight on after breakfast.
cases.weightAnswer: Four or five kilos. Just a shirt, towel and soft things.
cases.metalAnswer: No tools, no electronics. I travel light.
cases.packingAnswer: Everything is under the straps. Nothing loose or powered.
cases.responseAnswer: The clothes must have settled. The road has been rough tonight.
cases.authorReasoning: Carrier: 12.9 kg conflicts with the confident light-load claim; delayed sustained corrective pulse conflicts with strapped soft clothing. Two independent contradictions.

cases.name: 10_FalseToolboxCarrier
cases.contentsAnswer: Machine fitter. Replacement spanners and sockets for the morning shift.
cases.weightAnswer: Eleven kilos. The tool case is on my job sheet.
cases.metalAnswer: Steel tools, almost the whole case. The handle is the only plastic part.
cases.packingAnswer: Individual slots, trays bolted down. I do not let tools bounce around.
cases.responseAnswer: A latch can rattle. There are no springs or moving units in the load.
cases.authorReasoning: Carrier: 10.8 kg is plausible, but metal about 9/100 conflicts with an almost entirely steel load. Clear delayed pulse further contradicts fixed tool trays.

cases.name: 11_UnsecuredRadioCarrier
cases.contentsAnswer: Some books and my uncle's old radio. He listens to the same station every morning.
cases.weightAnswer: Ten or eleven kilos. Most of the weight is books.
cases.metalAnswer: The radio has a metal cover. The rest is paper and cloth.
cases.packingAnswer: The radio is loose. Unplugged, batteries out. No motor or wound mechanism.
cases.responseAnswer: It can knock once against the books. There should not be another movement after the first knock.
cases.authorReasoning: Carrier with a plausible cover: 10.5 kg and modest metal fit. The pulse produces delayed sustained corrective movement, contradicting a passive loose radio with no powered/wound source. No tilt test required.

cases.name: 12_LockedGimbalCarrier
cases.contentsAnswer: Camera gear for a property survey. It includes a stabilizer; I have the travel checklist.
cases.weightAnswer: Thirteen kilos, case included. I weighed it before leaving.
cases.metalAnswer: Brackets, lenses, the usual. Not a case full of metal.
cases.packingAnswer: Battery removed. Transport pin fitted. The moving stage is locked solid.
cases.responseAnswer: Foam can tremble, but that locked stage cannot pull back after a push.
cases.authorReasoning: Carrier: 12.9 kg and moderate metal fit. The explicit locked/unpowered explanation contradicts a clear delayed corrective pulse. Same broad response as innocent case 08, different packing claim.

cases.name: 13_StaticSamplesCarrier
cases.contentsAnswer: Display samples for a shop window. Hollow display shells, in foam. The real goods arrive next week.
cases.weightAnswer: Five kilos at most, including the bag. There is no solid merchandise in it.
cases.metalAnswer: No metal. They are painted hollow shapes, not working equipment.
cases.packingAnswer: Firmly wedged in foam. I do not want the painted surfaces touching.
cases.responseAnswer: It ought to be quiet. Nothing loose, no mechanism.
cases.authorReasoning: Quiet carrier: 11.8 kg conflicts with the confident lightweight hollow-display claim. Low metal and an almost still pulse do not exonerate it. Does not require removed balance test; false certainty would still be a player error.

cases.name: 14_PackedBatteryCarrier
cases.contentsAnswer: A spare battery and a few hand tools. Emergency kit. I like being prepared.
cases.weightAnswer: Roughly eight kilos in the hard case.
cases.metalAnswer: Some metal in the tools and battery, with plenty of foam.
cases.packingAnswer: Everything clamped into fitted foam. No liquid containers or moving machinery.
cases.responseAnswer: That must be a loose latch. It should make one little rattle and stop.
cases.authorReasoning: Carrier: 7.8 kg and moderate metal fit. Clear delayed movement lasting several seconds conflicts with the rigid dry load and single-latch explanation. Innocent water case 04 gives a matching explanation instead.
